Draft is in `CHANGELOG.md:3`. Here's what I found and the calls I made.

**The shape of it:** 380 commits, 126 merged PRs. 153 chore, 73 refactor, 64 test, 33 ci, 20 docs — that's 90% of the log and none of it reaches a user. What's left: 1 feat, 26 fix, 10 perf.

**The one new thing:** `feat(webhooks): retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff` (395fb48). It touched `src/webhooks/dispatch.js` *and* `src/core/config.js`, which suggests it added a config knob — you'll want to name the option and its default in the entry. I couldn't get the name from the log.

**Three things I'd call breaking, none of them labeled as such:**

- `stop re-exporting the internal error types` — 8 commits across core, db, auth, billing, jobs. The authors called them "internal," but re-exports are reachable, and anyone doing `instanceof` on them breaks silently on upgrade. This is the one most likely to bite.
- `refactor(api): drop the unused v1 export route` (56dc828) — filed as a refactor, but it touched `router.js`, `handlers.js`, and the API tests. "Unused" means unused by *us*.
- `fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403` (1d2bd55) — a correct fix, but clients branching on the status code will change behavior.

I put all three under Breaking because a user upgrading is the one who finds out. If you know the v1 route and the error types were never public, demote them — but that's a call from knowledge I don't have here.

**Two things I could not verify, both worth a check before you ship:**

- **Minimum Node version.** Five `docs: note the minimum node version` commits plus `ci: run the suite on node 22`, but every one of them only touched README/docs files. No commit in the log touches `engines` in `package.json`. So either the floor moved and the manifest wasn't updated, or the docs are describing a floor that was already there. If it moved, that's a Breaking entry and I've left it out. Worth one look at `package.json`.
- **Perf.** Ten commits — batched metric writes, skipped JSON round-trips, a reused parsed schema. I left all of them out. Your heading set is Breaking/Added/Fixed with no Performance heading, and none of the commits carry a number. "Faster" with nothing behind it isn't something someone installing the package would notice. If you have benchmark figures, `perf(api): reuse the parsed schema between requests` (9f02d92) is the one most likely to show up in real traffic.

Two caveats on the whole thing: this directory has `history/` and `CHANGELOG.md` but no source tree, so every line above is read off commit subjects and diffstats — I read no diffs. And the last commit is 2026-06-17, ten weeks before today, so if work continued elsewhere it isn't in this log. I dated the release 2026-08-28 for tomorrow's cut.

The Fixed list is deduped by symptom, not by commit — "guard the null cursor in the paginator" landed four separate times in queue, api, webhooks, and db, and a user experiences that as one bug.
